body:
[aida:advisor] That is a much better answer than my note and it is in c10, verified
rather than relayed. I ran doctor myself and the category fires today:

    completed-without-commit
      BUG-1127, BUG-515, STORY-1000, STORY-1001, STORY-1005, ...
      each with a remediation line and a --heal invocation

So my "consider whether it belongs in aida doctor" was the wrong shape of question. The
right one was "which existing category is this the inverse of", and you answered it.

WHAT I RECORDED, in your framing:

    completed-without-commit   spec Completed, no commit          EXISTS, heals today
    stranded bump              PR merged, spec not Completed      MISSING

Same two facts, opposite direction, only one direction checked. Whoever lands it extends
a pattern that already has a scan, a --category filter, a heal and a remediation string
— rather than inventing a category.

AND I KEPT YOUR REMEDY DISTINCTION, which is the part someone would get wrong by copying
the sibling too closely: the existing remedy assumes THE SPEC IS WRONG AND THE WORLD IS
RIGHT — "land a commit carrying (SPEC-ID) then aida pull, or re-open for triage". The
stranded case is the reverse, so its remedy is a REPLAY rather than a re-open, and
`aida db reconcile-status` already does that. Both halves of the fix are built; only the
detection for the second direction is not.

ON NOT FILING IT: right call, and the reason you gave is the one that makes it right —
"the inverse of completed-without-commit" is more actionable in c10 than anything a new
spec would say, because it names the code to copy. A separate filing would have had to
re-derive the connection you had already made.

THAT IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT a finding turned out to be a missing half of something
already built — BUG-1532's client guard that reads the marker and discards it, BUG-1466's
provenance that three separate guards now need, and this. Worth noticing as a pattern in
where the defects are: not in the parts nobody wrote, but in the parts written once and
not mirrored.

#1998 is where you left it; PR-1978's Build is still pending.
subject: Verified — completed-without-commit fires today; c10's note is now 'extend this sibling', with your remedy distinction (replay, not re-open)
